design:
Tier 2 (light). Hazard: a version history for dashboards adds a table and three columns, and the operator's :8000 Hub runs that migration on its real database at the first restart after this lands. The migration creates the new table `dashboard_versions` and adds three columns with defaults to slice 1's `dashboards` table (`version`, `edited_by`, `edited_at`, plus `panel_status`, see the contract); it deletes and rewrites no existing row's data, existing dashboards becoming version 1. Rollback is its downgrade dropping the table and the added columns, which loses only edit history and last-run errors, never a dashboard's name, description or panels. This slice builds after first-dashboard, so its migration follows that slice's in the revision chain.

Migration ordering: the migration's number is not fixed in this document. The builder takes it at build time from master's head (`git ls-tree master hub/hub/migrations/versions/`; the head was 0170_the_pr_s_ci_is_read_on_the_head.py when this was written, PR slice 2's 0169 and 0170 are already on master), names the file `NNNN_dashboards_edit_history.py` and points its down-revision at that head. Whichever of this slice, ask-any-agent-for-a-dashboard-and-get-one-that-stays (slice 1) and any other pending migration merges second renumbers after the other and re-points its down-revision before landing; this slice also needs slice 1's `dashboards` table, so it cannot merge before slice 1 does.

Decisions (the author's choice unless an open question says otherwise):
- Edit in place, by operation: the edit tool takes the dashboard's identifier, the version the agent read, and a list of operations (add panel, remove panel, change a panel's title, query or chart kind, move a panel, rename or re-describe the dashboard). Rejected: replacing the whole dashboard on every change, which is the failure this slice exists to remove. Slice 1's replace-whole save stays for creating, but a replace is also an edit: it bumps the version and keeps what it replaced, so it cannot be used to bypass history.
- Every edit is validated like a save in slice 1 (chart kind in the fixed set, never-queryable boundary, project boundary; the queries are not run), and the dashboard is unchanged if any operation is refused: an edit applies whole or not at all.
- Each dashboard carries a version number that goes up on every edit. An edit that names an older version than the current one is refused with the current dashboard returned, so the agent re-reads and re-applies.
- The Hub keeps the version an edit replaced; undo restores it as a new edit (so undo can itself be undone by asking). Depth: one step, see open questions.
- A dashboard's read answers, per panel, the last error or warning seen when it was run, so a repair needs no re-run to find the cause. The error is only known once the dashboard (or the panel) has been run, so a repair starts from an opened dashboard; an agent that finds no error for a panel runs its query with run_dashboard_query.

THE CONTRACT (binds to slice 1's names: table `dashboards`, panel `{id, title, query, kind}` with `id` `pnl-<12 hex>`, routes under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/dashboards`, tools save_dashboard / list_dashboards / read_dashboard / run_dashboard_query, events dashboard_saved / dashboard_deleted):

Columns added to `dashboards`: `version` Integer not null default 1; `edited_by` String(32) nullable (the agent's name from the run credential, or `operator` for an undo pressed on the screen; never taken from the request body); `edited_at` timestamp nullable (null until first edit); `panel_status` JSON not null default `{}` mapping panel id to `{"error": null | {"code": str, "message": str}, "warning": null | str, "at": timestamp}`, written by the Hub each time the run route (`GET .../dashboards/{dashboard_id}/run`) runs a panel; writing it does not change `version`.

Table `dashboard_versions` (model `DashboardVersion`), at most one row per dashboard: `dashboard_id` String(64) primary key; `project_id` String(64) indexed (so the project-delete sweep reaches it with no code); `version` Integer (the version it held); `name`, `description`, `panels` as in `dashboards`; `edited_by`, `edited_at` of the edit that produced it. Every edit and undo overwrites the row with what it replaced. Deleting a dashboard (DELETE route) deletes its row explicitly.

Operations, elements of the edit's `operations` array, each `{"op": ..., ...}`:
- `{"op": "add_panel", "panel": {"title", "query", "kind"}, "position": int | null}` (null appends)
- `{"op": "remove_panel", "panel_id": str}`
- `{"op": "change_panel", "panel_id": str, "title": str?, "query": str?, "kind": str?}` (only the keys present change)
- `{"op": "move_panel", "panel_id": str, "position": int}`
- `{"op": "rename", "name": str}`
- `{"op": "set_description", "description": str}`

Routes (added to hub/hub/api/v1/dashboards.py):
- `PATCH /dashboards/{dashboard_id}` body `{"base_version": int, "operations": [Operation]}` -> 200 dashboard with `version` + 1. Refusals: 409 `{"detail": {"code": "stale_version", "message": str, "current": <dashboard>}}`; 422 `{"detail": {"code": "operation_refused", "operation_index": int, "message": str}}` (including `invalid_chart_kind` and `not_queryable` reasons in the message, and an unknown `panel_id`); 404 for another project's dashboard.
- `POST /dashboards/{dashboard_id}/undo` -> 200 dashboard (the previous version's content, `version` + 1, `edited_by` the actor); 409 `{"detail": {"code": "nothing_to_undo"}}` when no row exists.
- `PUT /dashboards/{dashboard_id}` (slice 1) takes an optional `base_version`; when present it is checked like an edit's.
- Dashboard JSON (read, list, run, edit responses) gains `version: int`, `edited_by: str | null`, `edited_at: timestamp | null`, `can_undo: bool`; the stored read gives each panel `last_error: {"code","message"} | null` and `last_warning: str | null` from `panel_status`; the run route's panel entries already carry `error` and `warning`.

Agent tools (hub/hub/mcp_server.py, `@_tool()`): `edit_dashboard(dashboard_id: str, base_version: int, operations: List[Dict])` and `undo_dashboard(dashboard_id: str)`; `read_dashboard` returns the added fields. Finding the dashboard by name is `list_dashboards` plus the tool guidance (match by name; on none, several, or no name and none open, ask the operator which one and call nothing that writes). Both new tool names are added to the Copilot MCP allowlist in hub/hub/copilot_acp.py.

Events: `dashboard_edited`, payload `{"id": str, "name": str, "version": int}`, broadcast after commit by edit and undo, so an open screen refreshes.

Open dashboard context (provisional, bound by the open question): the conversation turn carries `open_dashboard_id` when the conversation is started from the Dashboards screen; the builder confirms where the conversation start carries context before the screen task starts.

UI: Undo button on the screen shown only when `can_undo`; the edited-by line reads `edited_by` and `edited_at`; hooks in hub/ui/src/api/dashboards.ts (`useUndoDashboard`) invalidate `['project', projectId, 'dashboards']`.

Guards and tests this change touches: the project-delete sweep test (hub/tests/test_project_delete_api.py) is satisfied because `dashboard_versions.project_id` exists; slice 1's tests in hub/tests/test_dashboards.py that compare a dashboard's exact JSON are relaxed to allow the four added fields (version, edited_by, edited_at, can_undo); the Copilot allowlist and the tools/list surface test as in slice 1.

CURRENT (slice 1): save(name, description, panels) -> dashboard; read; list; delete; run.
PROPOSED: edit(dashboard, base_version, operations[]) -> dashboard at version+1 | refused(reason, current); undo(dashboard) -> dashboard at version+1; read adds version, edited-by, edited-at and per-panel last error.

open_questions.question: How deep is undo? Options: one previous version (restore it, and restoring is itself undoable), or a full history the operator browses. Recommended (Architect): keep the previous version only, one step of undo; a browsable history is a later slice if it is missed.

How does the agent know which dashboard is open when the operator says 'this one'? Options: the conversation turn carries the identifier of the dashboard open on the Dashboards screen; or the agent only works by name and asks otherwise. Recommended (Architect): the turn carries the open dashboard's identifier (open_dashboard_id) when the conversation is started from the screen, with asking as the fallback; the builder must confirm the conversation can carry it before the screen task starts. Until settled, ac-open-one is not reachable.

On a stale edit, should the Hub refuse, or merge when the two edits touch different panels? Recommended (Architect): refuse and return the current dashboard (simple, never loses an edit); merging is not worth it for dashboards edited a few times a day.

problem: After slice first-dashboard (not yet built; see spec/changes/ask-any-agent-for-a-dashboard-and-get-one-that-stays/spec.json, non-goals) an agent can only save a new dashboard or replace one whole. Asked "add a panel for X" it has two bad choices: create a second dashboard that duplicates the first, or rewrite the whole thing from memory and risk silently altering panels the operator liked. A panel that breaks after a Hub upgrade, which that slice surfaces but does not repair, stays broken until someone rewrites the dashboard. This slice makes a saved dashboard something the operator keeps refining by asking.

requirements.rationale: A second near-duplicate dashboard per request is the failure the roadmap slice exists to remove.
requirements.statement: Asked to change an existing dashboard, an agent edits that saved dashboard: afterwards the project holds the same number of dashboards, the dashboard keeps its identity, and the Dashboards screen shows the change on the dashboard the operator already had.

requirements.rationale: Guessing between two dashboards edits the wrong one without anyone noticing.
requirements.statement: The agent edits the dashboard the operator means: the one named in the request, or when none is named the one open on the Dashboards screen; when the name matches no dashboard, or several, or none is named and none is open, the agent says so and asks which, and changes nothing and creates nothing.

requirements.rationale: The operator trusts a dashboard they have looked at; an edit that quietly rewrites other panels breaks that.
requirements.statement: An edit changes only what was asked: every panel, query, title, chart kind, the order of panels, the name and description that the request did not mention are unchanged after the edit.

requirements.rationale: A half-applied edit leaves a dashboard nobody asked for.
requirements.statement: The Hub applies an edit as a list of operations (add a panel, remove a panel, change a panel's title, query or chart kind, move a panel, rename or re-describe the dashboard); if any operation is refused, including a chart kind outside the fixed set or a panel that does not exist, no operation is applied and the refusal says which and why.

requirements.rationale: An agent works from what it read at the start of a long turn; the operator or another agent may have edited since.
requirements.statement: An edit made against a version of the dashboard that is no longer the current one is refused with a message saying the dashboard changed and the current dashboard, and nothing is overwritten.

requirements.rationale: Asking for changes is only safe if a wrong one costs one click.
requirements.statement: After an edit the Hub keeps the version it replaced, and the operator can restore it in one step from the Dashboards screen (and an agent can when asked); restoring is itself an edit, so it can be undone the same way; a dashboard with no earlier version offers nothing to restore.

requirements.rationale: Slice first-dashboard surfaces a broken panel but cannot mend it; this is the other half.
requirements.statement: A dashboard read tells the agent, for each panel, the error or warning its last run produced; asked to fix a broken panel, the agent can correct that panel's query from its error, check the new result, and save only that panel, after which the panel draws.

requirements.rationale: The edit path must not become a way round the query boundary.
requirements.statement: An edit's queries are held to the same limits as slice first-dashboard's queries (current project only, read-only, never-queryable data refused), and an agent cannot edit, undo or read the versions of a dashboard belonging to another project.
Deleting a dashboard, or the project it belongs to, removes its kept earlier version.
The Dashboards screen shows who last edited the dashboard and when, beside the author and date.

in_scope: An agent tool to edit a saved dashboard in place by operations, with the version it read
Finding which dashboard the operator means: by name, or the one open on the Dashboards screen
Refusing a stale edit and returning the current dashboard
Keeping the replaced version and one step of undo, on the Dashboards screen and for agents
A dashboard read that shows each panel's last error so an agent can repair a panel by asking
Recording who last edited a dashboard and when, shown on the screen
non_goals: Full version history, browsing or diffing old versions (one previous version only)
Several agents or people editing at once with merging; a stale edit is refused, not merged
The operator editing panels by hand on the screen (changes are asked for)
Changing the query tool, the chart kinds, or the queryable data from slice 1
Fixing a panel's query automatically without being asked
Sharing, exporting, or copying dashboards between projects

summary: The operator asks an agent to change a dashboard that already exists (add a panel, change a chart, fix a broken query). The agent finds the right saved dashboard, changes only what was asked in place, and the operator sees the same dashboard updated, not a new one. A change made on top of a newer edit is refused rather than overwriting it, the previous version is kept so one step undoes an edit, and a panel whose query broke is repaired by the agent from the error the panel shows.
